text.tspan: People continue their journey in rainy weather.
When we change our plans, a little care can make the experience better. Planning and thinking about
First, a backup plan makes a change less disappointing. For example, we choose a museum when rain
makes the outdoor walk uncomfortable. This is a small thing that makes the day easier.
Second, telling other people early helps everyone adjust. For example, we send a clear message about
the new meeting place before anyone leaves home. We do not need a perfect day to do this well.
We can change our plans more easily when we prepare and notice other people. These simple steps
give us a useful place to start.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a focused main idea. Develop one supporting reason in each body paragraph, with a concrete
example. Conclude by connecting the two reasons without introducing a new argument. Use the structure as a model; write
about an experience of your own.
Try it. What two reasons support the main idea? Explain one example. (Model: The two reasons are that a backup plan
makes a change less disappointing and that telling other people early helps everyone adjust. One example is that we choose
a museum when rain makes the outdoor walk uncomfortable.)
